name: Priya Desai, High-Risk Antepartum Unit: DKA in pregnancy at 28 weeks, hypokalemia on insulin, fetal monitoring

caseMeta.title: High-risk antepartum unit: DKA in a 29-year-old at 28 weeks 2 days with type 1 diabetes (glucose 242, pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, BHB 5.4) after norovirus-like vomiting and a halved basal dose: potassium 3.2 on insulin (short hold with dextrose kept), Category II fetal tracing that clears as the mother is corrected, no emergent cesarean, morning low glucose, evening contractions and the betamethasone decision, discharge teaching (3 days, checkpoints at every 0700 and 1900)
caseMeta.studentLevel: BSN / ADN antepartum and obstetric (upper level)
learningObjectives: Recognize DKA in pregnancy at a lower glucose (242) and apply the adult protocol adapted for pregnancy: insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h (70 kg) without a bolus, dextrose from a glucose under 200 and kept running through any hold, goal glucose 110-160, and the resolution rule (BHB under 0.6 plus venous pH 7.3 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher).

Apply the peripheral potassium rule when the potassium falls to 3.2 on insulin: hold the insulin, KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders one at a time (never more than 10 mEq/h from all sources, potassium-free carrier while a rider runs), restart at 3.5 or higher with prescriber confirmation, and give glargine 2 hours before the drip stops.

Interpret the fetal heart rate tracing (baseline, variability, accelerations, decelerations, contractions, NICHD category) as maternal acidosis, volume and potassium are corrected; position left lateral; know why an emergent cesarean is not the treatment for a Category II tracing in maternal DKA.

Manage the pregnancy-specific points: lower baseline bicarbonate and pCO2 (and Winter's formula), preterm contractions with fetal fibronectin and cervical length, why betamethasone is withheld in type 1 diabetes, low glucose after a gastroenteritis, kick counts, sick-day and ketone rules, and VTE risk reasoning.

problems.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis in pregnancy (type 1 diabetes since age 12), moderate, at 28 weeks 2 days
problems.details: Glucose 242, venous pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26, BHB 5.4 at 0145; corrected sodium 136.3. She cut her glargine from 24 to 12 units and gave no lispro during 36 hours of vomiting. Insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h = 7 units/h from 0215 (no bolus); hourly POC glucose; dextrose added at glucose under 200. Resolves only with BHB under 0.6 plus venous pH 7.3 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher.

problems.name: Intrauterine pregnancy G1P0 at 28 weeks 2 days (EDD 03/20/2027); type 1 diabetes in pregnancy
problems.details: Blood type O positive, antibody screen negative, rubella immune; group B strep status not yet due. Penicillin allergy (childhood rash). Estimated fetal weight 1,180 g (54th percentile) 3 days ago; amniotic fluid index 14.2 cm. Left lateral position; aspirin 81 mg daily for preeclampsia prevention.

problems.name: Category II fetal heart rate tracing from maternal ketoacidosis
problems.details: Baseline 165, minimal variability, no accelerations, recurrent late decelerations with contractions every 3-4 minutes at 0135. Managed by correcting the mother (fluids, insulin with dextrose, potassium, left lateral position); no emergent cesarean (MFM).

problems.name: Hypokalemia on insulin with low magnesium: K 3.2, Mg 1.5 on the 0655 specimen
problems.details: K 4.1, 3.6, 3.2. Flat T waves with prominent U waves and QTc 478 ms on the 0710 ECG. Insulin held; two KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders one at a time with a potassium-free dextrose carrier (10 mEq/h maximum from all sources); magnesium sulfate 2 g; goal 4.0 or higher.

problems.name: Type 1 diabetes since age 12 (one prior DKA at 16); no retinopathy, nephropathy or neuropathy
problems.details: Home glargine 24 units at 2100 and lispro 1 unit per 8 g carbohydrate (about 8, 8 and 10 units) plus 1 unit per 30 mg/dL over 120; continuous glucose monitor. HbA1c 6.4% before pregnancy, 6.0-6.1% in the first two trimesters, 6.2% on admission.

orders.name: Full Code, maternal and fetal (husband Rohan Desai is the emergency contact)
Establish two peripheral IVs (18 gauge, left forearm and right antecubital; no central line). Assess every site hourly during infusions; remove when no longer needed
orders.instructions: IV A (left forearm) carries the carrier fluid and the insulin, each on its own pump channel; IV B (right antecubital) carries the potassium riders (and the magnesium after 0730). Priming volume is discarded and not counted as intake.

orders.name: Continuous external fetal heart rate monitoring and tocodynamometry while in ketoacidosis and for 24 hours after resolution (interpret and document the tracing every hour; notify the OB provider for any change in category). Do NOT proceed to emergent cesarean delivery for a Category II tracing during maternal ketoacidosis: treat the mother (fluids, insulin with dextrose, potassium, left lateral position) and reassess
orders.instructions: Maternal-fetal medicine directive. Intrauterine resuscitation: left lateral position, correct the acidosis, no routine oxygen while maternal SpO2 is 95% or higher. Call for a prolonged deceleration, recurrent late decelerations returning, minimal variability for over 1 hour after the first improvement, or a heart rate that stays under 110 or over 160.

orders.name: Maternal positioning: left lateral recumbent, or 30-degree left tilt (wedge under the right hip), whenever in bed; sequential compression devices on both legs while in bed; bathroom with assistance
orders.instructions: Avoid lying flat on the back (aortocaval compression). VTE risk was assessed as low: see the admission note. Reassess the risk score daily.

orders.name: Continuous 5-lead telemetry through Day 3 0700; vital signs every hour while on the insulin infusion, then every 4 hours; strict intake and output (Foley urometer hourly while on the insulin infusion); daily weight at 0700 on the same scale
orders.instructions: Notify for urine under 35 mL/h for 2 hours, new crackles or oxygen need, headache or visual change, systolic BP 140 or higher or diastolic 90 or higher, vaginal bleeding or leaking of fluid, or contractions more often than every 5 minutes.

orders.name: ECG 12-lead now (tachycardia, ketoacidosis, electrolytes pending); acquire 0145, interpretation released 0155

Initial labs at 0145: venous blood gas, BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, beta-hydroxybutyrate, lactate, CBC, hepatic panel, lipase, uric acid, HbA1c; urinalysis. Repeat chemistry, venous gas, BHB, magnesium and phosphorus at 0400 and again with the 0700 panel. POC glucose hourly from the insulin start. Blood type O positive, antibody screen negative, rubella immune (prenatal record): no Rh immune globulin needed

orders.name: insulin regular (HUMULIN R) 100 units in 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL (1 unit/mL) infusion - DKA in pregnancy
orders.frequency: Continuous (adult DKA protocol adapted for pregnancy); HOLD for K under 3.5
orders.instructions: Regular insulin 100 units in NS to 100 mL (1 unit/mL) on its own pump channel, 7 units/h, NO bolus. Independent two-nurse check of drug, concentration and rate at initiation and every change. POC glucose hourly, including any hold. HOLD at once for K under 3.5, glucose under 70 or urgent deterioration, KEEP the dextrose carrier running, and notify. Restart only when K is 3.5 or higher AND the prescriber confirms. Insulin titration (POC glucose every hour): glucose under 200 with K 3.5 or higher = D5 carrier (already running) and insulin 0.05-0.1 unit/kg/h; pregnancy goal on the infusion is 110-160 mg/dL. Glucose under 110: change the carrier to D10 0.45% NaCl at the same rate (keep K rules) and call the prescriber; keep the insulin running while ketones persist. Falling more than 100 mg/dL in an hour: call for a rate review. Glucose under 70: hold the insulin, treat with the hypoglycemia order, check every 15 minutes and call. DKA is resolved ONLY when beta-hydroxybutyrate is under 0.6 AND (venous pH 7.30 or higher OR bicarbonate 18 or higher); a normal glucose or a closed anion gap alone is not enough. Final stop only with the transition order and the glargine overlap.
orders.rationale: 70 kg (current pregnant weight) x 0.1 unit/kg/h = 7 units/h; no bolus. Started at 0215 after the first potassium (4.1, above 3.5) was known. The infusion is HELD for any K under 3.5 for as short a time as possible (insulin drives potassium into cells) and restarted as soon as K is 3.5 or higher and the prescriber confirms, at 0.05 unit/kg/h with dextrose running, because the fetus is acidemic and ketones are still high.
nursingConsiderations: Hourly POC glucose; strict I&O; telemetry; continuous fetal monitoring.
High-alert drug: two-nurse check of drug, concentration, rate and patient.
Stop only by order, after the first subcutaneous basal insulin dose has had its overlap.

medication.importantInfo: Insulin moves potassium into cells: the blood level can fall quickly within hours. Ketones and acid-base decide when insulin stops, not the glucose number.

orders.name: POTASSIUM SAFETY PROTOCOL: two peripheral IVs; never more than 10 mEq/h from ALL sources; one KCl 10 mEq/100 mL rider at a time with a potassium-free carrier; no 40 mEq/L bags; carrier with KCl 20 mEq/L only when no rider is running; HOLD insulin if K is under 3.5 (keep the dextrose running); goal K 4.0 or higher; continuous telemetry
orders.instructions: PERIPHERAL POTASSIUM SAFETY PROTOCOL (two peripheral IVs, no central line; pregnancy, goal K 4.0 or higher on insulin): before ANY potassium, confirm urine output of at least 0.5 mL/kg/h (35 mL/h at 70 kg) and review the latest creatinine. TOTAL IV potassium from ALL sources on ALL lines must NEVER exceed 10 mEq per hour. While a KCl rider runs the carrier fluid must be POTASSIUM-FREE (D5 0.45% NaCl, no added KCl): swap the 20 mEq/L bag for the potassium-free carrier BEFORE the rider starts (the 20 mEq/L carrier gives 5 mEq/h at 250 mL/h and 4 mEq/h at 200 mL/h) and hang the 20 mEq/L bag again only after the last rider. Riders are premixed KCl 10 mEq in 100 mL over 1 hour on a pump, ONE at a time, never in parallel, never IV push; no 40 mEq/L bags (central-line strength). K above 5.0 = no potassium, recheck in 2-4 hours. K 3.5-3.9 = one or two sequential riders with the potassium-free carrier, then the 20 mEq/L carrier again. stickyNotes.title: Potassium: peripheral IVs, 10 mEq/h limit

notes.title: OB Triage Admission Note - Vomiting, Deep Breathing and Decreased Fetal Movement at 28 Weeks
notes.author: B. Montenegro, MD
notes.summary: 29-year-old G1P0 at 28 weeks 2 days with type 1 diabetes, 36 hours of vomiting after a classroom norovirus exposure, who cut her basal insulin in half. Kussmaul respirations, sinus tachycardia, fruity breath; fetal tracing Category II. Two IVs, Foley, labs sent, 1,000 mL saline and ondansetron started; left lateral tilt.
notes.body:
**HPI**
29-year-old G1P0 at 28 weeks 2 days (EDD 03/20/2027 by an 8-week crown-rump length), type 1 diabetes since age 12 on multiple daily injections and a continuous glucose monitor, who arrived at 0130 with her husband Rohan. Pupils in her fourth-grade classroom had gone home with acute viral gastroenteritis two days ago. About 36 hours ago she developed nausea and watery diarrhea (3 stools, resolved) and then intractable non-bloody vomiting (8 episodes in 18 hours). Her sensor read 175-235 mg/dL, which she did not recognize as dangerous; she feared a low, cut her bedtime glargine from 24 to 12 units last night and gave no mealtime lispro while sipping ginger ale and water. At 0030 she developed epigastric soreness, deep sighing breathing and marked fatigue, and noticed less fetal movement over the last 4 hours.

**Exam**
Anxious, nauseated, alert and oriented x4. Dry mucous membranes, fruity ketotic breath, deep regular Kussmaul respirations, sinus tachycardia, no fever. Lungs clear. Abdomen: gravid, soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding; uterus soft between mild contractions. Placed at once in a 30-degree left lateral tilt (wedge under the right hip). Oxygen is not applied: saturation is 99% on room air and hyperoxia is avoided.

**Fetal monitoring (started 0135)**
External Doppler: baseline 165 bpm, minimal variability, no accelerations, recurrent late decelerations after mild contractions every 3-4 minutes. NICHD Category II.

**Actions**
Two 18-gauge peripheral IVs (left forearm, right antecubital) and a Foley catheter with urometer at 0145 (120 mL of dark amber urine; dipstick ketones 4+, glucose 3+, specific gravity 1.030, nitrite and leukocytes negative). Blood drawn for venous gas, BMP, beta-hydroxybutyrate, magnesium, phosphorus, lactate, CBC, hepatic panel and lipase (epigastric pain at 28 weeks: pancreatitis and HELLP syndrome must be excluded; blood pressure is normal). 12-lead ECG at 0145. Sodium chloride 0.9% 1,000 mL over 1 hour from 0150 (about 14 mL/kg at 70 kg) and ondansetron 4 mg IV at 0155 for retching. Maternal-Fetal Medicine and Endocrinology are being called now.

**Impression**
Suspected diabetic ketoacidosis in pregnancy with a Category II fetal tracing from maternal acidosis and volume depletion. Plan: confirm with labs, start insulin once the potassium is known, treat the mother first, continuous fetal monitoring, no emergent delivery for the tracing alone.

notes.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation - DKA in Pregnancy with a Category II Tracing
notes.author: L. Aldrich, MD
notes.summary: Moderate DKA at a glucose of only 242 (pregnancy lowers the glucose at which ketoacidosis appears). Category II tracing from maternal acidosis. No emergent cesarean: correct the mother, left lateral, dextrose with the insulin.
notes.body:
**Reason for consultation**
Diabetic ketoacidosis at 28 weeks 2 days with a Category II fetal tracing.

**Assessment**
The 0145 labs show moderate DKA at a glucose of only 242 mg/dL: venous pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26 and beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.4. Pregnancy lets ketoacidosis develop at lower glucose values because of continuous fetal and placental glucose use, placental hormone insulin resistance, vomiting and a lower renal threshold for glucose, and because the baseline bicarbonate (18-22) and pCO2 (27-32) are already lower from progesterone-driven hyperventilation, which leaves less buffering reserve. Winter's formula (expected pCO2 23 +/- 2) was derived in non-pregnant adults; her measured pCO2 of 24 is appropriate compensation and, because pregnancy lowers the baseline, the pregnancy expectation is a few mmHg lower still. Maternal ketoacids and hydrogen ions cross the placenta, and a fetus is more acidemic than its mother, which explains the tracing (baseline 165, minimal variability, recurrent late decelerations).

**Recommendations**
1. Do NOT proceed to emergent cesarean delivery for this Category II tracing. Delivering a 28-week fetus from an acidotic mother raises maternal risk and delivers an acidemic, preterm infant. Intrauterine resuscitation by correcting the maternal acid-base, volume and potassium status almost always restores a Category I tracing within hours.
2. Left lateral position at all times; fluids as ordered; no routine oxygen.
3. Add 5% dextrose to the fluids as soon as the glucose is under 200 so the fetus has a steady carbohydrate supply while the insulin clears the ketones. If the potassium forces an insulin hold, keep the dextrose running.
4. Continuous fetal monitoring until 24 hours after resolution. Call me for a prolonged deceleration, a return of recurrent late decelerations or a change of category.
5. Neonatology counseling when she is stable. Blood type is O positive: no Rh immune globulin.

notes.title: Endocrinology Consultation - DKA in Pregnancy Triggered by Gastroenteritis and Insulin Reduction
notes.author: H. Dalgaard, MD
notes.summary: DKA from vomiting and a halved basal dose. Corrected sodium 136.3; pCO2 24 matches Winter's 23 +/- 2. Insulin 7 units/h; POC 192 at 0300, so D5 with KCl 20 mEq/L was added; peripheral potassium limit 10 mEq/h from all sources.
notes.body:
**Assessment**
29-year-old woman, 28 weeks 2 days, type 1 diabetes, in DKA triggered by viral gastroenteritis with vomiting and a self-reduced basal dose (12 instead of 24 units) and no mealtime insulin. HbA1c 6.2%.

**Arithmetic (0145 panel)**
- Anion gap 134 - 98 - 10 = 26
- Corrected sodium 134 + 1.6 x (242 - 100)/100 = 136.3
- Winter's expected pCO2 1.5 x 10 + 8 = 23 +/- 2: measured 24. In pregnancy the baseline pCO2 is lower, so the pregnancy expectation sits a few mmHg below Winter's value; she is compensating appropriately, with no respiratory acidosis.
- Venous pH 7.24 (Henderson-Hasselbalch from bicarbonate 10 and pCO2 24).

**Treatment so far**
1,000 mL saline from 0150 to 0250; regular insulin 7 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h at 70 kg, no bolus) from 0215. The 0300 glucose is 192 (242 at the start), so at 0300 the fluid changed to D5 0.45% NaCl with KCl 20 mEq/L at 250 mL/h: glucose under 200 in pregnancy triggers dextrose so the fetus has continuous substrate and the insulin can run at full dose to clear the ketones.

**Rules for the rest of the stay**
- Peripheral IVs only: through a peripheral line potassium is limited to 10 mEq/h from ALL sources, in separate riders one at a time. While a rider runs the carrier must contain no potassium. No 40 mEq/L bags.
- Potassium under 3.5: hold the insulin, keep the dextrose running, replace, restart at 3.5 or higher with the prescriber.
- DKA is resolved only when beta-hydroxybutyrate is under 0.6 and the venous pH is 7.30 or higher or the bicarbonate is 18 or higher; basal insulin goes in 2 hours before the drip stops.
- Goal glucose on the infusion 110-160 mg/dL.
BMP, gas and ketones are repeated at 0400 and with the 0700 panel.

notes.title: Pharmacy Note - Insulin, Potassium Limit and Antiemetic Safety
notes.author: G. Aoki, PharmD
notes.summary: 70 kg dosing weight; insulin 7 units/h verified. K 3.6 at 0400: one 10 mEq rider 0420-0520 on IV B with the carrier changed to potassium-free so the total stays at 10 mEq/h (the 20 mEq/L bag alone is 5 mEq/h). Ondansetron acceptable; hold if K or QTc is abnormal.
notes.body:
Reviewed the weight-based orders for Priya Desai (70.0 kg current weight, 28 weeks 2 days). Regular insulin is running at 7 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h), no bolus, which limits the early drop in potassium and the osmotic shift. The 0400 panel (released 0415): glucose 178 mg/dL, sodium 135, potassium 3.6, chloride 101, bicarbonate 12, anion gap 22, pH 7.30, pCO2 25, beta-hydroxybutyrate 4.1.

Potassium plan checked against the peripheral rule (never more than 10 mEq/h from all sources): the carrier was D5 0.45% NaCl with KCl 20 mEq/L at 250 mL/h, which delivers 5 mEq/h. A rider of 10 mEq/h on top would reach 15 mEq/h, so at 0420 the carrier is changed to D5 0.45% NaCl without potassium at 150 mL/h for the hour of the rider (KCl 10 mEq/100 mL on IV B, 0420-0520). The total is exactly 10 mEq/h and the total IV volume stays 250 mL/h. The 20 mEq/L bag resumes at 0520. Urine output is 110-150 mL/h, well over 35 mL/h.

Ondansetron 4 mg IV is acceptable in the third trimester; it can lengthen the QT interval, so repeat doses are PRN only and are held while the potassium is under 3.5 or the QTc is over 470 ms. Next panel with the 0700 draw.

**Measurements**

**Interpretation**

Recorded at 0710 after the critical potassium of 3.2 mEq/L with magnesium 1.5 mg/dL (insulin infusion running since 0215). The pattern fits insulin-driven hypokalemia with low magnesium. QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron) should be avoided until potassium and magnesium are corrected. Repeat when the potassium has been replaced.

notes.title: High-Risk Antepartum Unit Admission History and Physical
notes.author: B. Montenegro, MD
notes.summary: 29-year-old G1P0 at 28 weeks 2 days with type 1 diabetes and DKA from gastroenteritis; K 3.2 and Mg 1.5 on insulin: insulin held, dextrose kept, riders and magnesium started; Category II tracing improving; VTE risk low, sequential compression devices, no enoxaparin; aspirin 81 mg continues.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Vomiting, deep breathing and decreased fetal movement; admitted from OB triage with DKA in pregnancy.

**HPI**
See the triage notes. Type 1 diabetes since age 12, one prior DKA at 16 (influenza), HbA1c 6.4% before pregnancy and 6.0-6.1% in the first and second trimesters (6.2% today). Gastroenteritis with 36 hours of vomiting, glargine cut from 24 to 12 units, lispro omitted. Triage labs: glucose 242, bicarbonate 10, gap 26, venous pH 7.24, BHB 5.4, K 4.1. Insulin 7 units/h since 0215; D5 with potassium from 0300; one KCl rider 0420-0520. The 0655 panel (released 0705): glucose 152, **K 3.2 (critical)**, Mg 1.5 (below the pregnancy range 1.6-2.2), phosphorus 2.4, bicarbonate 14, gap 18, pH 7.34, pCO2 27, BHB 2.8. ECG at 0710 pending.

**Obstetric history**
G1P0, spontaneous conception, EDD 03/20/2027 (8-week crown-rump length). Nuchal translucency and cell-free DNA low risk (46,XX), anatomy scan at 20 weeks normal, fetal echocardiogram at 22 weeks normal. Growth scan 3 days ago: estimated fetal weight 1,180 g (54th percentile), amniotic fluid index 14.2 cm. Blood type O positive, antibody screen negative, rubella immune, RPR non-reactive, hepatitis B surface antigen negative, HIV negative, group B strep not yet due (36 weeks).

**PMH, medicines, social, family**
No retinopathy (eye exam 4 months ago), no nephropathy (baseline creatinine 0.55; 24-hour urine protein 110 mg), no neuropathy. Home: glargine 24 units at 2100, lispro 1 unit per 8 g carbohydrate (about 8, 8 and 10 units) with a correction of 1 unit per 30 mg/dL over 120, aspirin 81 mg daily (preeclampsia prevention since 12 weeks), prenatal vitamin, continuous glucose monitor on the right upper arm. **Allergy: penicillin (childhood maculopapular rash), low-risk history.** Husband Rohan (31), at the bedside; fourth-grade teacher; no tobacco, alcohol or drugs. Mother: hypothyroidism and celiac disease; father: hypertension and hyperlipidemia; maternal aunt: type 1 diabetes.

**Exam (arrival)**
Tired, alert, mildly weak in the calves, nausea much better, no vomiting since 0140. Dry mucous membranes improving, deep slightly fast breathing, lungs clear, no JVD, trace pedal edema, soft gravid uterus, mild epigastric tenderness, reflexes 2+. Weight 70.0 kg (pre-pregnancy 62.0 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 25.7 now). Fetal tracing: Category II (see the 0715 interpretation).

**Assessment and plan**
1. **DKA in pregnancy, moderate, improving** (glucose 152, gap 18, BHB 2.8). Resolution needs BHB under 0.6 plus pH 7.30 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher.
2. **Hypokalemia 3.2 with low magnesium on insulin:** hold the insulin now, keep the dextrose carrier (D5 0.45% NaCl without potassium, 100 mL/h), KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders at 0715 and 0815 one at a time (the carrier must be potassium-free so no minute exceeds 10 mEq/h), magnesium sulfate 2 g over 2 hours from 0730, ECG now, repeat BMP, gas and BHB when rider 2 ends (0915). Planned hold about 2 hours, not longer: ketones are still high and the fetus is acidemic. Restart at 3.5 units/h (0.05 unit/kg/h) when K is 3.5 or higher and I confirm.
3. **Fetal status:** Category II improving; continuous monitoring; left lateral; no emergent cesarean (MFM agrees).
4. **VTE risk assessment:** age 29, BMI 25.7, no prior clot or thrombophilia, no major immobility; transient factors are pregnancy, admission and dehydration. Low risk with a short stay and walking from tomorrow: sequential compression devices while in bed, hydration, no enoxaparin (pregnancy is a risk factor, but this does not justify drug prophylaxis here; a possible early delivery would also complicate neuraxial anesthesia timing). Reassess daily.
5. **Aspirin 81 mg continues** (with a sip, once nausea has settled); prenatal vitamin from Day 2; ondansetron only as needed with QTc and potassium checked.
6. NPO except ice chips and sips with medicines until nausea has settled; Foley for hourly urine.
7. Penicillin allergy noted. GBS is not yet due.

notes.author: M. Doyle, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: Guilt about halving her basal insulin; four sick-day rules reviewed: never stop basal insulin, sip carbohydrate, check blood ketones, call early; ketone meter ordered for her bedside.
notes.body: Held a 45-minute session with Priya and Rohan. Priya said she "caused this by cutting my glargine in half and skipping lispro when my sensor was only in the 190s and 220s." notes.body:
Called to evaluate Mrs. Desai at 28 weeks 3 days for regular contractions every 4 minutes lasting 45 seconds after the afternoon walk (the tracing is Category I, see the 1925 interpretation). Exam at 1845: sterile speculum, closed visually, no pooling, ferning or nitrazine change; the **rapid fetal fibronectin swab was taken first, before any other contact** (it is valid at 24-34 weeks with intact membranes and no recent intercourse, bleeding or digital exam); then transvaginal ultrasound. Results (released 1900): **fibronectin negative; cervical length 3.8 cm, closed internal os, no funneling.** A cervical length of 3.0 cm or longer is itself reassuring and, with a negative fibronectin, the chance of delivery within 7-14 days is well under 1-2%. The 1830 panel (released 1900) shows bicarbonate 21, anion gap 11, BHB 0.2: no recurrent ketoacidosis; urine screen pending.

**Impression:** benign uterine irritability after exertion and recent dehydration, not preterm labor. With oral hydration and left lateral rest the contractions have already spaced to every 10-12 minutes by 2000.

**Antenatal corticosteroids: NOT given.** They are for women in whom delivery within 7 days is likely. In type 1 diabetes betamethasone causes profound hepatic glucose output and insulin resistance beginning 6-12 hours after the dose and lasting up to 5 days, usually needing a 30-40% (sometimes more) insulin increase or an insulin infusion with hourly glucose and ketone checks to avoid a second DKA. Triggers to reconsider: cervical length under 2.0 cm, or 2.0-2.9 cm with a positive fibronectin, rupture of membranes, advanced cervical change, or bleeding. If true preterm labor were diagnosed: group B strep status is unknown, so prophylaxis would be cefazolin (childhood penicillin rash is a low-risk allergy history); magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks. I explained all of this to her and Rohan.

notes.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Day 3 Note - Biophysical Profile and Surveillance Plan
notes.author: L. Aldrich, MD
notes.summary: BPP 8/8 on the four ultrasound components (10/10 with the reactive NST) at 0830, 28w4d; monitoring changed to a 20-minute tracing every 4 hours; daily kick counts; outpatient testing weekly then twice weekly from 32 weeks.
notes.body:
Performed a bedside ultrasound and biophysical profile at 0830 (28 weeks 4 days, about 38 hours after biochemical resolution): fetal breathing movements over 30 seconds (2 points), at least 3 body or limb movements (2), normal tone (2), amniotic fluid maximum vertical pocket 5.4 cm with an AFI of 13.8 cm (2): **8/8 on the ultrasound components; 10/10 including the reactive non-stress test.** She has had a Category I tracing for over 36 hours with normal acid-base, so continuous monitoring is changed to a 20-minute tracing every 4 hours while awake and once overnight until discharge. Daily fetal kick counts after dinner in left lateral position (goal 10 movements in 2 hours, usually 15-30 minutes).

**After discharge:** weekly NST and fluid checks from now (29-31 weeks), twice-weekly NST with AFI or BPP from 32 weeks, growth ultrasound every 4 weeks. Delivery timing will be individualized by me at the clinic visits from her glucose control, fetal growth and any complications (usually 37-39 weeks for type 1 diabetes). First visit Monday at 0900 with an NST.

notes.title: Endocrinology Day 3 Progress Note
notes.author: H. Dalgaard, MD
notes.summary: Targets met on glargine 20 units and 1:10 lispro: 0300 91, fasting 92, 1 hour after breakfast 134. Sensor and fingerstick agree within 4-6 mg/dL now; hypoglycemia plan reviewed.
notes.body: Good control over the last 24 hours on glargine 20 units at 2100 and lispro 1 unit per 10 g: 0300 91, fasting 92 (goal under 95), 1 hour after breakfast 134 (goal under 140); BHB 0.1, bicarbonate 21. Her own continuous glucose monitor was compared with simultaneous point-of-care values: during dehydration and acidosis on Day 1 the interstitial readings can lag blood glucose by 10-15 minutes, which is why hourly fingersticks were required on the infusion; now that she is euvolemic its readings are within 4-6 mg/dL. Reminder: confirm any reading under 70 or any symptom that does not match with a fingerstick. Endocrinology clinic Monday at 1030 with the sensor data and ketone log. Expect insulin needs to rise through the third trimester; we will titrate at each visit. Medically ready for discharge tomorrow morning after one more night of observation and teach-back.

notes.title: Diabetes Educator Teach-Back - Ketone Meter and Nasal Glucagon
notes.author: M. Doyle, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: Return demonstration with the blood ketone meter (0.1 mmol/L at 1330) and nasal glucagon; action thresholds recited correctly: under 0.6 normal, 0.6-1.4 call, 1.5 or more or vomiting go to OB triage.
notes.body: Delivered the bedside supplies and watched Priya check her blood ketones at 1330: **0.1 mmol/L** (glucose 129 mg/dL one hour after a lunch with lispro 7 units). She recited the thresholds: **under 0.6 mmol/L** normal; **0.6-1.4** drink fluid, take the sick-day correction, recheck glucose and ketones in 2 hours and **call the endocrinology or MFM on-call line**; **1.5 or more, or any ketones with more than one vomit, abdominal pain or deep breathing: go directly to OB triage.** Rohan demonstrated giving nasal glucagon 3 mg for a severe low when she cannot swallow safely. Both showed full understanding of the four rules from yesterday.

notes.title: Perinatal Social Work Note - Work, Follow-Up and Support
notes.author: L. Nwosu, LCSW
notes.summary: Worry about missing teaching days and classroom viral illness; medical excuse letter through the end of the week; transportation, insurance and family support confirmed; MFM 0900 and endocrinology 1030 Monday.
notes.body: Met with Priya and Rohan. She is worried about missing four days of teaching and about returning to a classroom with circulating gastroenteritis. We completed a medical excuse letter for her principal through the end of this week, with recommendations for water and snack breaks, scheduled glucose checks and strict handwashing in her room. Transportation, commercial health insurance (covering insulin, sensors and ketone strips) and nearby family support (her parents 15 minutes away) were confirmed. Two linked appointments: Maternal-Fetal Medicine and a non-stress test on Monday 01/04 at 0900, then Endocrinology in the same building at 1030.

notes.title: Dietitian Follow-Up Note
notes.author: R. Trevino, RDN
notes.summary: Diary review: 1-hour glucose after meals 124-134, no morning low; sample home menus built around her food preferences; written plans given.
notes.body: Reviewed her food and glucose diary. Spacing carbohydrate across 3 meals and 3 snacks (breakfast 60 g, snack 15, lunch 70, snack 15, dinner 80, bedtime 30 with protein), her one-hour post-meal glucoses were 124-134 mg/dL and there has been no morning low since Day 2. She chose a 3-day home menu around her own foods (smaller portions of brown basmati rice or whole-wheat roti with dal, paneer, grilled chicken and non-starchy vegetables). Written copies of the 2,200 kcal plan and her sick-day liquid carbohydrate chart were given. No further nutrition barriers.

notes.title: Obstetric Evening Note - Ready for Final Night
notes.author: B. Montenegro, MD

The 1900 NST was reactive and the kick count normal (see the 1935 interpretation). notes.title: Obstetric and Maternal-Fetal Medicine Discharge-Readiness Note
notes.author: B. Montenegro, MD and L. Aldrich, MD
notes.summary: 28 weeks 5 days, discharge planned about 0900: well-grown singleton, Category II tracing resolved to Category I within about 9 hours of treatment with no cesarean; contractions Day 2 benign (cervical length 3.8 cm, fibronectin negative, no steroids); BPP 8/8; today NST reactive; glucose 88.
notes.body: Priya is ready for discharge home today at 28 weeks 5 days with a viable, well-grown singleton. Her triage Category II tracing (baseline 165, minimal variability, recurrent late decelerations) improved with maternal correction of volume, acid-base and potassium and reached Category I at about 1100 on Day 1, avoiding an unnecessary and risky preterm cesarean. The Day 2 evening contractions were benign uterine irritability (cervical length 3.8 cm, closed; fetal fibronectin negative), so betamethasone and its risk of steroid-induced recurrent DKA were avoided. The biophysical profile on Day 3 was 8/8 and the 0630 non-stress test this morning is reactive. Labs at 0700: fasting glucose 88, sodium 136, potassium 4.2, chloride 104, bicarbonate 21, creatinine 0.52, anion gap 11, BHB 0.1, phosphorus 3.6, magnesium 2.0; urine ketones negative; hemoglobin 10.8 (expected physiologic dilution of pregnancy). Rh positive: no immune globulin. GBS testing at 36 weeks. Education completed: daily kick counts, preterm labor and preeclampsia warning signs, sick-day return criteria; teach-back by both without error. Both IVs to be removed with intact sites before she leaves. Follow-up Monday 01/04 at 0900 (MFM, NST, fluid check) and 1030 (endocrinology).

notes.title: Endocrinology Discharge Note
notes.author: H. Dalgaard, MD
notes.summary: DKA in pregnancy resolved on Day 1 (glucose 242, pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, BHB 5.4 at presentation); one fasting low on the full basal dose; home regimen glargine 20 units, lispro 1:10 plus scale; ketone meter and glucagon in hand.
notes.body:
Priya was admitted with DKA at a glucose of only 242 mg/dL (pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26, BHB 5.4) from gastroenteritis, a halved basal dose and omitted mealtime insulin. Treatment: crystalloid, regular insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h with dextrose from a glucose under 200, potassium and magnesium replacement through peripheral IVs within the 10 mEq/h limit, a 2 hour 20 minute insulin hold for a potassium of 3.2 with dextrose kept, and biochemical resolution on the 1850 draw of Day 1 (pH 7.42, bicarbonate 19, anion gap 12, BHB 0.5), with a 2-hour overlap with glargine. One fasting low (62) on Day 2 led to glargine 20 units. Since then fasting 91-92 and 88 and 1-hour postprandial values 124-134, with BHB 0.1.

**Discharge regimen:** glargine 20 units at 2100; lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate 10-15 minutes before meals (about 6, 7 and 8 units) plus a correction of +1 for 121-150, +2 for 151-180, +3 for 181-210; aspirin 81 mg daily; prenatal vitamin; ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 hours as needed; nasal glucagon 3 mg; blood ketone meter; continuous glucose monitor. Pregnancy targets: fasting under 95, 1 hour under 140, 2 hours under 120, bedtime 90-120. I expect to raise doses with the third trimester. Clinic Monday at 1030.
